claims.claim: Export of services by an osek murshe is zero-rated (0% VAT) under Section 30 of the Israeli VAT Law, legally distinct from exempt (patur, Sec 31). In the Green Invoice API a 0% line is set via the income-row vatRate field (decimal 0), not a vatType value; the document-level vatType enum (DocumentVatType) is 0=Default, 1=Exempt, 2=Mixed at both document and row level.
claims.raw_snippet: vatType 0 Default, 1 Exempt, 2 Mixed; vatRate decimal e.g. 0.18; export zero-rated 0% Section 30 סעיף 30 not exempt

claims.claim: Official Green Invoice / Tax Authority / Bank of Israel reference URLs cited by the skill (all live; gov.il is bot-blocked to curl but renders for humans)

Illustrative calculation example values internal to the skill, NOT external regulatory claims: a NIS 10,000 net service totals NIS 11,800 with 18% VAT; in the withholding example the client withholds NIS 2,000 and remits NIS 9,800 in cash, and the two payment lines (9,800 + 2,000) sum to the 11,800 document total.
claims.raw_snippet: Internal arithmetic example; 10000 * 1.18 = 11800, and 9800 + 2000 = 11800. Not an external claim.

claims.claim: The Morning API exposes POST /suppliers and POST /expenses. An expense created with an attached file first becomes an expense draft that must be approved before it counts as an actual expense; an expense created without a file is created immediately.
claims.raw_snippet: With a file (such as a receipt or invoice) - the upload first becomes an expense draft. Review the draft, then approve it to turn it into a regular expense. A draft is simply a pending expense waiting for your approval; until then, it isn't counted as an actual expense.
